items.rationale: The failed indoor heating pipe falls under §2.4.3 if escape-of-water cover is scheduled. Under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9, the estimate uses plain copper at about €15/m for 6.4 m, payable only if that full length was necessary.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow necessary fittings at standard copper prices, not the chrome premium. Four elbows at €10 each track Case 40.
Sections 7.1.8(e) and 7.1.9 allow only fittings of the size and quantity needed for the documented repair. If all five were needed, the Case 40 standard copper benchmark is about €20 each.
Sections 7.1.8(e) and 7.1.9 limit payment to a necessary, correctly sized fitting at standard grade. The Case 40 copper equivalent supports €20.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers minor fixings used in the repair. The matched prior gives 8 × €1.10 = €8.80.
Section 7.1.8(e) excludes materials whose dimensions do not match the documented repair, and no 10 mm pipe is identified. If a necessary matching use is established, allow about 4 × €5.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary supports if they fit the repaired installation under §7.1.8(e). The matched Case 40 prior is €25 for four.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for the necessary repair, but §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9 exclude time spent solely on upgrades and additions. The matched gross benchmark for 6.75 hours is €595.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper time, not labour solely attributable to the upgrades or new installations. The matched Case 40 prior is €418 for 5.75 hours.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit reimbursement to the pre-loss rock-wool equivalent. Case 40 supports about €120 for six standard insulation pieces.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers binding wire as a consumable to the extent it is attributable to the covered repair or its standard insulation equivalent. The matched prior gives 2 × €9.80 = €19.60.
Section 7.1.9 excludes installations that were not present before the loss; this permanent sensor is not a diagnostic service used to locate the leak. €95 is a hypothetical gross price only.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the valve because there was no pre-loss valve to replace. €110 is a hypothetical gross price only.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow a lump sum for minor repair consumables, provided it does not duplicate other charges. The matched gross prior is €36.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge per contractor per invoice. This is the only such charge, so the matched gross prior of €79 applies.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of material removed from the insured repair. The matched prior is €60 gross, with no separate disposal limit stated.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes general processing charges added to itemised labour and materials. €25 is a hypothetical gross fee only.
